headline: Waste reduction means not creating trash in the first place—the most effective form of waste management
universal_truth: Prevention beats cure; avoiding problems is better than solving them; the best cleanup is not creating the mess
fun_facts: The average American generates about 4.5 pounds of trash per day—1,600 pounds per year
Reducing waste saves more resources than recycling—prevention beats processing
Package-free stores are growing worldwide—proving products don't need excessive packaging
discussion_questions: What 'waste' do you create that could be prevented entirely?
Where are you solving problems you could avoid creating?
How do you design waste out of your systems?

hook.script: Recycling is good, but not creating waste is better. The most effective trash management is never generating the trash. Prevention beats processing—the cleanest garbage is the garbage that never existed.

cliff.script: We focus on recycling and disposal, but reduction is more powerful. Why do we overlook prevention?

options.text: Cleanup is visible, prevention is invisible—we notice problems solved, not problems prevented; but avoiding a mess is always better than cleaning it up
options.response: Yes. Recycling programs get publicity. Not buying unnecessary things goes unnoticed. But prevention saves more resources than any processing. The best solution often happens before the problem.
Recycling handles existing waste, but reduction prevents it—which uses less energy and resources...

fact1.title: Hierarchy of Solutions
fact1.script: Reduce, reuse, recycle—in that order. Reduction prevents waste. Reuse extends life. Recycling processes what remains. Start with the most effective strategy, not the easiest.

fact2.title: Design Out Waste
fact2.script: Smart design eliminates waste before it's created. Products designed for longevity, packaging designed to minimize, processes designed for efficiency. Prevention is a design choice.

fact3.title: Personal Prevention
fact3.script: You create waste too—wasted time, wasted effort, wasted money. Before figuring out how to handle waste, ask how to not create it. Prevention beats cure in every domain.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Prevention beats cure. Avoiding problems is better than solving them. The best cleanup is not creating the mess.

outro.script: That's Day 279. Tomorrow, we'll explore using things again—reuse. Until then, identify waste you could prevent entirely.

growTrack.title: Prevention Check - What Waste Could You Avoid?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify waste to prevent rather than manage
growTrack.activity: What 'waste' do you regularly create—in time, money, energy, things? Could any of it be prevented entirely? Before solving problems, ask if you could avoid creating them. Prevention is the first and best solution.
